metadata.title: Formalisation in the Lean theorem prover of the relation between corner-free sets and communication complexity

nodes.name: Forgetting a coordinate
nodes.statement: For an index $i : [d]$, we define \begin{align} \mathrm{forget}_i : G^d & \to G^{\{j : [d] \mid j \ne i\}} \\ x & \mapsto j \mapsto x_j \end{align}
nodes.label: def:forget

nodes.name: Forbidden pattern
nodes.statement: We say a tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_d) : (G^d)^d$ is a {\bf forbidden pattern with tip $v : G^d$} if $$a_{i, j} = v_j$$ for all $i, j$ distinct. We also simply say $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$ is a {\bf forbidden pattern} if it is a forbidden pattern with tip $v$ for some $v$.
nodes.label: def:forbidden-pattern

nodes.name: Multidimensional corner
nodes.statement: A {\bf multidimensional corner} in $d$ dimensions is a tuple of the form $(x, x + ce_1, \dots, x + ce_d)$ for some $x : G^d$ and $c : G$, where $ce_i$ is the vector of all zeroes except in position $i$ where it is $c$. Such a corner is said to be {\bf trivial} if $c = 0$.
nodes.label: def:multicorner

nodes.name: Corner-free number
nodes.statement: The {\bf $d$-dimensional corner-free} number of $G$, denoted $r_d(G)$ is the size of the largest set $A$ in $G^d$ such that $A$ doesn't contain a non-trivial corner.
nodes.label: def:corner-free-num

nodes.name: Corner-coloring number
nodes.statement: The {\bf $d$-dimensional corner-coloring number} of $G$, denoted $\chi_d(G)$, is the smallest number of colors one needs to color $G^d$ such that no non-trivial $d$-dimensional corner is monochromatic.
nodes.label: def:corner-color-num

nodes.name: Lower bound on the corner-coloring number
nodes.statement: $$r_d(G) \chi_d(G) \ge N^d$$
nodes.label: lem:corner-num-lower

nodes.statement: Find a coloring of $G^d$ in $\chi_d(G)$ colors without non-trivial monochromatic $d$-dimensional corners. The coloring partitions $G^d$ into $\chi_d(G)$ sets of size at most $r_d(G)$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on the corner-coloring number
nodes.statement: $$r_d(G) \chi_d(G) \le 2d N^d \log N$$
nodes.label: lem:corner-num-upper

nodes.statement: Find $A$ a corner-free set of density $\alpha = r_d(G)/N^d$. If we pick $m > d\log N/\alpha$ translates of $A$ randomly, then the expected number of elements not covered by any translate is $$N^d(1 - \alpha)^m \le \exp(dN - m\alpha) < 1$$ Namely, there is some collection of $m$ translates of $A$ that covers all of $G^d$. Since being corner-free is translation-invariant, this cover by translates gives a coloring in $m$ colors without non-trivial monochromatic corners. So $$\chi_d(G) \le m \le 2d \log N/\alpha = 2d N^d \log N/r_d(G)$$ if we set eg $m = \left\lfloor d\log N/\alpha\right\rfloor + 1$.

nodes.name: NOF protocol
nodes.statement: A {\bf NOF protocol} $P$ consists of maps \begin{align} \mathrm{strat} : & [d] \to G^{d - 1} \to \mathrm{List} \mathrm{Bool} \to \mathrm{Bool} \\ \mathrm{guess} : & [d] \to G^{d - 1} \to \mathrm{List} \mathrm{Bool} \to \mathrm{Bool} \end{align}
nodes.label: def:protocol

nodes.name: NOF broadcast
nodes.statement: Given a NOF protocol $P$, the {\bf NOF broadcast on input $x : G^d$} is inductively defined by \begin{align} \mathrm{broad}(x) : \mathbb{N} & \to \mathrm{List} \mathrm{Bool} \\ 0 & \mapsto [] \\ t + 1 & \mapsto \mathrm{strat}_{t \% d}(\mathrm{forget}_{t \% d}(x), \mathrm{broad}(x, t)) :: \mathrm{broad}(x, t) \end{align}
nodes.label: def:broadcast

nodes.name: Length of a broadcast
nodes.statement: For every NOF protocol $P$, every input $x : G^d$ and every time $t$, $\mathrm{broad}(x, t)$ has length $t$.
nodes.label: lem:length-broadcast

nodes.statement: Induction on $t$.

nodes.name: Valid NOF protocol
nodes.statement: Given a function $F : G^d \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the NOF protocol $P$ is {\bf valid in $F$ at time $t$ on input $x$} if all participants correctly guess $F(x)$, namely if $$\mathrm{guess}_i(\mathrm{forget}_i(x), \mathrm{broad}(x, t)) = F(x)$$ for all $i : [d]$.
nodes.label: def:valid-protocol

nodes.name: The trivial protocol
nodes.statement: For all $F$, we define the {\bf trivial protocol} by making participant $i$ do "Send the $t / d$-th bit of the number of participant $i + 1$" and "Compute $x_i$ from the binary representation given by participant $i - 1$, then compute $F(x)$".
nodes.label: def:trivial-protocol

nodes.name: The trivial protocol is valid
nodes.statement: For all $F$, the trivial protocol for $F$ is valid in time $d\left\lceil \log_2 n\right\rceil$.
nodes.label: lem:trivial-protocol-valid

nodes.statement: Obvious.

nodes.name: Deterministic complexity of a protocol
nodes.statement: The {\bf communication complexity of a NOF protocol $P$ for $F$} is the smallest time $t$ such that $P$ is valid in $F$ at time $t$ on all inputs $x$, or $\infty$ if no such $t$ exists.
nodes.label: def:det-protocol-complex

nodes.name: Deterministic complexity of a function
nodes.statement: The {\bf deterministic communication complexity of a function} $F$, denoted $D(F)$, is the minimum of the communication complexity of $P$ when $P$ ranges over all NOF protocols.
nodes.label: def:det-fun-complex

nodes.name: Trivial bound on the function complexity
nodes.statement: The communication complexity of any function $F$ is at most $d\left\lceil \log_2 n\right\rceil$.
nodes.label: lem:trivial-bound-det-fun-complex

nodes.statement: The trivial protocol is a protocol valid in $F$ in time $d\left\lceil \log_2 n\right\rceil$.

nodes.name: The tip of a monochromatic forbidden pattern
nodes.statement: Given $P$ a NOF protocol and a time $t$, if $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$ is a forbidden pattern with tip $v$ such that $\mathrm{broad}(a_i, t)$ equals some fixed broadcast history $b$ for all $i$, then $\mathrm{broad}(v, t) = b$ as well.
nodes.label: lem:mono-forbidden-pattern-tip

nodes.statement: Induction on $t$. TODO: Expand

nodes.name: $\eval$ function
nodes.statement: The {\bf $\mathrm{eval}$ function} is defined by \begin{align} \mathrm{eval} : G^d & \to \mathrm{Bool} \\ x & \mapsto \begin{cases} 1 & \text{ if } \sum_i x_i = 0 \\ 0 & \text{ else} \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: def:eval

nodes.name: Forbidden patterns project to multidimensional corners
nodes.statement: If $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$ is a forbidden pattern such that $\mathrm{eval}(a_i) = 1$ for all $i$, then $$(\mathrm{forget}_i(a_1), \dots, \mathrm{forget}_i(a_d))$$ is a multidimensional corner for all index $i$.
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: lem:forbidden-pattern-project-multicorner

nodes.statement: Let $v$ be the tip of $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$. Then, using that $\sum_k a_{j, k} = 0$ and $v_k = a_{j, k}$ for all $k \ne j$, we see that $v_j = a_{j, j} + \sum_k v_k$. This means that $(\mathrm{forget}_i(a_1), \dots, \mathrm{forget}_i(a_d)$ is a multidimensional corner by setting $x = \mathrm{forget}_i(a_i)$ and $c = \sum_k v_k$.
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Monochromatic forbidden patterns are trivial
nodes.statement: Given $P$ a NOF protocol valid in time $t$ for $\mathrm{eval}$, all monochromatic forbidden patterns are trivial.
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: lem:mono-forbidden-pattern-trivial

nodes.statement: Assume $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$ is a monochromatic forbidden pattern with tip $v$, say $\mathrm{broad}(a_i, t) = b$ for all $i$. By Lemma \ref{lem:mono-forbidden-pattern-tip}, we also have $\mathrm{broad}(v, t) = b$. Since $P$ is a valid NOF protocol for $\mathrm{eval}$, we get $\mathrm{eval}(a_i) = \mathrm{eval}(v)$ for all $i$, meaning that $(a_1, \dots, a_d) = (v, \dots, v)$ is trivial.
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Lower bound for $D(\eval)$ in terms of $\chi_d(G)$
nodes.statement: $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \ge \lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil$$
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: thm:det-fun-complex-eval-ge-corner-color-num

nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a protocol valid in time $t$ for $\mathrm{eval}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:mono-forbidden-pattern-trivial}, $\mathrm{broad}(\cdot, t)$ is a coloring of $\{x \mid \sum_i x_i = 0\}$ in at most $2^t$ colors (since $t$ bits were broadcasted) such that all monochromatic forbidden patterns are trivial. By Lemma \ref{lem:forbidden-pattern-project-multicorner}, this yields a coloring of $G^{d - 1}$ in at most $2^t$ colors such all monochromatic corners are trivial. Hence $2^t \ge \chi_d(G)$, as wanted.
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Lower bound for $D(\eval)$ in terms of $r_d(G)$
nodes.statement: $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \ge d\log_2\frac N{r_d(G)}$$
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: cor:det-fun-complex-eval-ge-corner-free-num

nodes.statement: Putting Theorem \ref{thm:det-fun-complex-eval-ge-corner-color-num} and Lemma \ref{lem:corner-num-lower} together, we get $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \ge \left\lceil \log_2\frac{2dN^d\log N}{r_d(G)}\right\rceil \ge d\log_2\frac N{r_d(G)}$$
nodes.section: 3 Lower bound on the communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: The non-monochromatic protocol
nodes.statement: Given a coloring $c : \{x \mid \mathrm{eval} x = 1\} \to [C]$, writing $a_i$ the vector whose $j$-th coordinate is $x_j$ except when $j = i$ in which case it is $-\sum_{j \ne i} x_j$, we define the {\bf non-monochromatic protocol for $c$} by making participant $i$ do ``Send the $t / d$-th bit of $c(a_i)$ until time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil$, then send $1$ iff $c(a_i)$ agrees with the broadcast from time $1$ to time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil$ read as a color'' and ``Send $1$ iff the broadcasts from time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil$ to time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil + d$ were all $1$''.
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: def:non-monochromatic-protocol

nodes.name: The non-monochromatic protocol is valid
nodes.statement: If $c$ is a coloring such that all monochromatic forbidden patterns are trivial, then the non-monochromatic protocol for $c$ is valid in time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil + d$.
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: lem:non-monochromatic-protocol-valid

nodes.statement: We have $$\text{answer is } 1 \iff \text{ all $a_i$ have the same color } \iff \text{ all $a_i$ are equal } \iff \sum_i x_i = 0$$ where the first equivalence holds by definition, the second one holds by assumption and the third one holds since the $a_i$ form a forbidden pattern.
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Upper bound for $D(\eval)$ in terms of $\chi_d(G)$
nodes.statement: $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \le \lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil + d$$
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: thm:det-fun-complex-eval-le-corner-color-num

nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{lem:forbidden-pattern-project-multicorner}, find some coloring $c$ of $\{x \mid \sum_i x_i = 0\}$ in $\chi_d(G)$ colors such that all monochromatic forbidden patterns are trivial. Then Lemma \ref{lem:non-monochromatic-protocol-valid} tells us that the non-monochromatic protocol for $c$ is valid in time $\lceil\log_2\chi_d(G)\rceil + d$.
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Upper bound for $D(\eval)$ in terms of $r_d(G)$
nodes.statement: $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \le 2d\log_2\frac N{r_d(G)}$$
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}
nodes.label: cor:det-fun-complex-eval-le-corner-free-num

nodes.statement: Putting Theorem \ref{thm:det-fun-complex-eval-le-corner-color-num} and Lemma \ref{lem:corner-num-upper} together, we get $$D(\mathrm{eval}) \le \left\lceil \log_2\frac{2dN^d\log N}{r_d(G)}\right\rceil \le 2d\log_2\frac N{r_d(G)}$$
nodes.section: 4 Upper bound on the deterministic communication complexity of \texorpdfstring{$\eval$}{eval}

nodes.name: Randomised complexity of a protocol
nodes.statement: The {\bf communication complexity of a randomised NOF protocol $P$ for $F$ with error $\epsilon$} is the smallest time $t$ such that $$\mathbb P(x \mid P \text{ is not valid at time } t) \le \epsilon$$ or $\infty$ if no such $t$ exists.
nodes.label: def:rand-protocol-complex

nodes.name: Randomised complexity of a function
nodes.statement: The {\bf randomised communication complexity of a function $F$ with error $\epsilon$}, denoted $R_\epsilon(F)$, is the minimum of the randomised communication complexity of $P$ when $P$ ranges over all randomised NOF protocols.
nodes.label: def:rand-complex

nodes.name: The randomised equality testing protocol for $\eval$
nodes.statement: The {\bf randomised equality testing protocol for $\mathrm{eval}$} has domain $\Omega := (\mathrm{Bool}^d)^{\lceil\log_2\epsilon^{-1}\rceil}$ with the uniform measure and is defined by making participant $i$ do ``Compute $$a_{i, k} = \sum_{j \ne i} \omega_{j, k}x_j$$ and send the sum of the digits of $a_{i, t/d}$ mod $2$ at time $t$'' and ``Guess $1$ iff the sum of the digits of $\omega_i x_i$ + what participant $i$ said is $0$ modulo $2$''.
nodes.label: def:rand-eq-test-protocol-eval

nodes.name: The randomised equality testing protocol for $\eval$ is valid
nodes.statement: The randomised equality testing protocol is valid for $\mathrm{eval}$ at time $2d$.
nodes.label: lem:rand-eq-test-protocol-eval-valid

nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{eval}(x) = 1$, then the protocol guesses correctly. Else it errors with probability $$2^{-\lceil{\log_2\epsilon^{-1}}\rceil} \le \epsilon$$

nodes.name: The randomised complexity of $\eval$ is constant
nodes.statement: $$R_\epsilon(\mathrm{eval}) \le 2d\lceil\log_2\epsilon^{-1}\rceil$$
nodes.label: thm:eval-rand-complexity

nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:rand-eq-test-protocol-eval-valid}, the randomised equality testing protocol is valid for $\mathrm{eval}$ at time $2d$.
